text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--The government's environmental tax package has caused political uproar, with the Socialist People's Party attacking fellow leftists the Unity List for blocking income tax increases and the government's Centre Democrat allies threatening revolt over the ruling coalition's alliance with the left.
--The Centre Democrats are not saying it publicly but are likely to ally themselves with the Liberals and Conservatives in the next election.

--Safety improvements on the Great Belt undersea tunnel are to increase operating costs tenfold from original estimates to around 10.4 million crowns a year, in addition to further capital investment of 3.8 million. POLITIKEN
--Economists say that the government's environmental tax package is a camouflaged attempt to boost state revenue and balance the budget, under the guise of environmental concerns.
--Danes and Swedes on both sides of the narrow Oeresund channel have won 100 million Danish crowns in EU aid for cross-border regions.
--The deregulation of Danish telecommunications has boosted growth in the electronics industry which could become the country's most important sector.
--The government, in alliance with the left, is preparing a further five billion crown tightening package, expected to hit property owners hard.
--The government's environmental tax package will cost 3,000 jobs, a leading retail organisation estimates.
-- The government and the left have a secret agreement to hold gross income tax at its current 8.0 percent.
